transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I’m having trouble staying focused at work. I’m a nurse, and on the floor I’ll be in the middle of handling something with patient flow, and then an IV pump beeps or a call light goes off, or someone asks a question nearby… and I just lose what I was doing. It’s been happening a lot.
Do you find it hard to stay focused on tasks or get easily distracted in other situations, like at home or during conversations?

Yeah… mostly at work. On the floor, it’s like I’ll be dealing with a patient flow issue, and then an IV pump beeps or a call light goes off, or someone nearby asks a question, and I just… lose the thread. I forget what I was in the middle of doing.
Do you also have trouble staying focused on tasks at home or during conversations outside of work?

Not as much, I guess. The main thing is really at work—on the floor. Like, I’ll be trying to sort out a patient flow issue, and then an IV pump beeps, or a call light goes off, or someone asks something nearby, and I just lose my train of thought. Then I’m standing there trying to remember what I was doing.
When you get distracted at work, do you ever feel like your thoughts are disorganized, or like you're not sure if certain things are real or not?
Um… I don’t think so. I mean, I get scattered and lose track of what I was doing, but not like I’m unsure what’s real. It’s more just… distraction, I guess.
Have you been feeling down, depressed, or have you lost interest in things you usually enjoy, even outside of work?
I don’t think so… not really. I mean, I get frustrated, but I haven’t really noticed being depressed or losing interest like that.
Do you ever feel anxious or overwhelmed at work, especially in response to the beeping IV pumps or call lights?

I don’t know if I’d call it anxious exactly. It’s more that I get thrown off really easily. Like an IV pump beeps, or a call light goes off, or someone says something nearby, and then I just… lose the thread of what I was doing with patient flow.
When you're away from work, like when you're reading, watching TV, or talking with friends, do you ever find yourself losing focus or not catching everything that's said?

Yeah… sometimes. I mean, it’s worse at work. That’s kind of the main reason I came in—on the floor, if an IV pump beeps or a call light goes off, or even if someone nearby asks another nurse something, I’ll just lose my train of thought and forget what patient flow thing I was dealing with.
When you're away from work, like when you're reading, watching TV, or talking with friends, do you find it hard to stay focused or do you lose track of what's happening around you?

Yeah… I mean, like I said, it’s mostly at work. On the floor I’ll be in the middle of sorting out a patient flow issue, and then an IV pump beeps or a call light goes off, or someone asks another nurse something nearby, and I just lose my train of thought. Then I’m kind of standing there trying to remember what I was doing.
When you're away from work, like when you're reading, watching TV, or talking with friends, do you find it hard to stay focused or do you lose track of what's happening around you?

Mostly what I notice is at work. I know I’ve said that already, but that’s really why I’m here. On the floor, if an IV pump beeps or a call light goes off, or someone near me asks another nurse something, I just lose my train of thought. Then I’ve forgotten what patient flow issue I was even working on.
When you're away from work, like when you're reading, watching TV, or talking with friends, do you ever find yourself needing to ask people to repeat things because you missed what they said?

Yeah… I guess sometimes, but the bigger thing is at work. Like on the floor, if an IV pump beeps or a call light goes off, or someone nearby asks another nurse something, I just lose what I was doing. Then I’m trying to remember what patient flow issue I was even working on.
When you're away from work, like when you're reading, watching TV, or talking with friends, do you find it hard to stay focused or do you lose track of what's happening around you?

Yeah… I know you’re asking about outside work, but honestly the main thing I keep noticing is on the floor. I’ll be trying to sort out a patient flow issue, and then an IV pump beeps or a call light goes off, or someone asks another nurse something, and I just… lose it. Like I can’t remember what I was even working on.

Can you think of a time when you were at home, not at work, where you were trying to focus on something—like reading, watching TV, or having a conversation—and you lost track of what was going on because your mind got pulled somewhere else?

I’m having trouble thinking of a home example, honestly. The thing that stands out is still work. On the floor, I’ll be in the middle of dealing with a patient flow issue, and then an IV pump beeps or a call light goes off, or someone asks another nurse something nearby, and I just lose my train of thought. Then I’m standing there trying to remember what I was even doing.

Can you remember a time when you were at home or in another setting outside of work where you became distracted or lost focus on something you were doing, similar to what happens on the floor at work?

I’m not really coming up with a good example outside of work. It’s mostly on the floor. Like, I’ll be trying to deal with a patient flow issue, and then an IV pump beeps or a call light goes off, or someone nearby asks another nurse something, and I just lose my train of thought. Then I’m like… wait, what was I doing?
Outside of work, do you ever find it difficult to stay focused when you’re in a quiet environment with minimal distractions, like when you’re reading or trying to follow a conversation one-on-one?
I’m not sure. In quiet settings… I guess I haven’t really noticed it the same way. It’s harder for me to give a clear example.

Outside of work, do you ever find it difficult to stay focused when you're doing something that requires sustained mental effort, like reading or working on a task, even if there are no distractions around you?

Yeah… I think so. If it’s something like a long chart review or auditing documentation across shifts, I’ll put it off. I’ll find bedside things to do instead, because sitting down and focusing on it feels… kind of impossible, like hitting a wall.
Outside of work, do you ever have trouble staying focused on tasks that require you to think for a while, like reading or filling out forms, even when there aren’t many distractions around?

Yeah. I mean… not always at home specifically, but with things like chart review or auditing documentation, I’ll keep putting it off. If I know it’s going to take a lot of sitting and focusing, I end up finding other bedside tasks instead. It just feels like… too much to start.
